paper.title_en: Correlations of the B4/2 anomaly with increased triaxiality and the borders of shape coexistence
paper.abstract_en: The B4/2 anomaly is defined in the literature for even-even nuclei as the ratio of the 4<math altimg="si27.svg"><mrow><msup><mrow/><mo>+</mo></msup><mo>→</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo></msup></mrow></math>/2<math altimg="si28.svg"><mrow><msup><mrow/><mo>+</mo></msup><mo>→</mo><msup><mn>0</mn><mo>+</mo></msup></mrow></math> transition strengths with values smaller than unity. This is a peculiar behavior that cannot be explained by standard collective models, including the three paradigms of nuclear structure: vibrational, rotational, or γ-soft, all of which predict B4/2 >  1. As new experimental data have emerged in recent years, we re-examine this pattern in even-even nuclei by summarizing all the experimental information available in the 28 ≤ Z ≤ 92 region. We find 17 isotopes for which the data indicate a clear B4/2 <  1 case. In addition, we compare these nuclei with the predictions of the proxy-SU(3) model, and show for the first time that enhanced triaxiality alone does not suffice to guarantee the presence of the B4/2 anomaly, with the proximity to the border of some region of shape coexistence appearing to also be a necessary condition.
